design_rationale: The SEND study explicitly randomised 250 eligible patients 1:1 to resection with or without elective neck dissection via a central telephone randomisation service using a minimisation program (a concurrent observational cohort was collected separately and analysed apart from the randomised comparison).

domain_judgments.rationale: Central randomisation with concealed allocation and minimisation stratified by age, T-stage and surgeon; baseline patient and tumour characteristics were balanced between the two randomised arms.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Allocation concealment was achieved using a central randomisation system. Patients were randomised (1:1 allocation) after research nurses telephoned Saving Faces, the trial co-ordinating centre. A minimisation computer program stratified patients by age..., tumour stage... and surgeon." ; "Patient characteristics (Table 1) and tumour characteristics (Supplementary Table 1) were balanced within the randomised patients."

domain_judgments.rationale: Open-label surgical trial in which 20/250 patients (8%) did not receive their allocated procedure (12 allocated END had resection only, 7 allocated resection had END), and although a primary ITT analysis was performed, the authors emphasise and interpret the per-protocol results, which are susceptible to bias from non-adherence.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In those randomised to have resection only, seven patients actually had a neck dissection as well and for another patient what they had was unreported. In those allocated to END, 12 had resection only. Excluding these 20 patients formed the perprotocol group."

domain_judgments.rationale: Survival outcomes were available for essentially all 250 randomised patients with long follow-up (median 57 months) and censoring at last known alive; attendance at assessment visits was similar between groups, though QoL/resource-use completeness is less fully reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Median follow-up was 57 months (25–75th centile 43–61 months). Similar numbers of patients in both trial groups attended each assessment visit."

domain_judgments.rationale: Overall survival is objective and insensitive to lack of blinding, but DFS/loco-regional recurrence and adverse events relied on unblinded local clinical assessment, local imaging/pathology "according to local practice" with no central or blinded adjudication, and QoL/adverse events were self- or clinician-reported in an open-label design.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Imaging for suspected locally recurrent, metastatic or new disease was arranged in the event of clinical suspicion or if the patient reported worrying symptoms. This was performed according to local practice."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a pre-specified primary outcome (OS), pre-specified per-protocol and subgroup analyses, but the non-significant primary outcome is de-emphasised in favour of secondary DFS/per-protocol results, multiple effect estimates are presented (up to 5 years vs all time points, adjusted/stratified, post-hoc AJCC 8th edition analyses), and recruitment was stopped early after inspection of accumulating data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "We also conducted analyses (not pre-specified) according to the AJCC 8th edition... In July 2015, the Independent Data Monitoring Committee (IDMC) recommended early termination of accrual because the preliminary data were consistent with the published Mumbai trial"

overall_summary: Allocation was centrally randomised with concealment and groups were balanced, and survival data were near-complete, but the open-label surgical design with 8% crossover (with heavy interpretive reliance on per-protocol analyses), locally assessed unblinded recurrence/adverse-event outcomes, early termination of accrual, and emphasis on secondary rather than the non-significant primary endpoint raise concerns in three domains. No domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is "some concerns".

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a multicenter prospective randomized trial in which patients were allocated to observation or elective selective neck dissection using two sets of sealed envelopes stratified by T classification.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation used stratified sealed envelopes and baseline characteristics were comparable (sex, age, T stage, grade all p>.4), but the sequence generation method is not described and envelopes are not stated to have been opaque, sequentially numbered, or centrally managed, leaving concealment uncertain.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Two sets of sealed envelopes, 1 set for T1 patients and another set for T2 patients, were used for the randomization of patients to either observation or elective neck dissection."

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding of surgical interventions is impossible and co-interventions differed (adjuvant radiotherapy was advised to pN+ patients, with 1 of 8 declining; 1 observation patient did not comply with the follow-up protocol), and one randomized patient was excluded post-randomization rather than analyzed by intention-to-treat; however the deviations are small and consistent with usual care.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "One clinically T2 patient who was randomized to the observation arm was found to have pathologic T3 and therefore was excluded."

domain_judgments.rationale: Survival and recurrence outcomes appear available for essentially all 71 analyzed patients with long and balanced follow-up in both arms, with no loss to follow-up reported.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the minimum follow-up duration of these 53 patients was 34 months (mean, 86 months; longest, 122 months). The median follow-up duration of patients was 92 months on observation arm and was 93 months for neck dissection arm."

domain_judgments.rationale: Mortality/disease-specific survival are objective outcomes, but surveillance differed between arms (observation patients received 3-monthly neck ultrasonography, detecting nodal events differentially) and outcome assessors were unblinded, and attribution of cause of death (node-related vs other) involves judgment that could be influenced by knowledge of allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The main outcome assessment parameter was node-related mortality... The secondary outcome assessment parameter was the 5-year tumor-specific survival rate."

domain_judgments.rationale: A protocol/registration exists but was posted in 2005, long after recruitment began in 1996 and near its end (2004), so prespecification of the primary outcome and analyses cannot be verified; the study was also underpowered relative to its own stated plan (power 0.70, n=71 of 72 planned), making the null findings vulnerable to interpretation bias.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The research protocol was posted to the website of clinical trial public information center of The University of Hong Kong for public access of information in 2005 ... clinical trial registration number HKCTR-17"

overall_summary: This small multicenter RCT had balanced baseline characteristics and near-complete long-term follow-up, but the randomization sequence generation and adequacy of sealed-envelope concealment are not described, surveillance and adjuvant treatment differed between unblinded arms, one randomized patient was excluded post-randomization, and registration occurred late (2005) relative to recruitment (1996–2004) in an underpowered trial reporting a null result. No single domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is some concerns.

design_rationale: Explicit random allocation: "Patients were randomly assigned to undergo either elective or therapeutic neck dissection in a 1:1 ratio with the use of a prepared computerized block design," with stratification and a registered protocol (NCT00193765).

domain_judgments.rationale: Computer-generated stratified block randomization in a 1:1 ratio with baseline characteristics well balanced across arms; although concealment of allocation is not explicitly described, the computerized sequence and balanced baselines suggest adequate process.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients were randomly assigned to undergo either elective or therapeutic neck dissection in a 1:1 ratio with the use of a prepared computerized block design... The two study groups were well balanced with respect to baseline characteristics"

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was impossible for a surgical trial and a small number of patients did not receive assigned surgery (6 operated elsewhere, 8 had no surgery), and co-intervention differed (more adjuvant radiotherapy in the elective arm, acknowledged by authors as a possible contributor), although an intention-to-treat analysis was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A higher percentage of patients in the elective-surgery group received adjuvant radiotherapy on the basis of nodal indications, and the contribution of this factor to the improved rate of overall survival cannot be excluded."

domain_judgments.rationale: Loss to follow-up was modest and similar between arms (10.3% vs 8.7%), but censoring of ~10% in a survival analysis with no sensitivity analysis reported, plus 19 recurrences categorized as "not known," leaves minor concern.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The numbers of patients who were lost to follow-up were similar in the two groups (25 of 243 patients [10.3%] in elective-surgery group and 22 of 253 patients [8.7%] in the therapeutic-surgery group)."

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome, all-cause overall survival, is objective and not susceptible to assessor bias; follow-up schedules and imaging were protocol-defined and uniformly supervised, though the secondary disease-free survival outcome depended on unblinded clinical detection of relapse.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The primary end point was overall survival, which was defined as the interval between the date of randomization and the date of death from any cause."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered with a published protocol and prespecified end points and alpha-spending, but an unplanned interim analysis was conducted, the trial was stopped early for benefit with reporting restricted to the first 500 of 596 randomized patients, and post hoc subgroup analyses were added — early stopping may overestimate effect size.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "An unplanned interim analysis (after the analysis of 248 patients and the occurrence of 43 deaths) was performed in 2011... In June 2014, the data and safety monitoring committee requested another interim analysis... we performed an analysis involving the first 500 patients who underwent randomization."

overall_summary: This well-conducted, registered, single-center randomized surgical trial used computerized stratified randomization, intention-to-treat analysis, and an objective primary outcome (all-cause survival), giving low risk in D1 and D4. Overall "some concerns" is driven by the unavoidable lack of blinding with differential adjuvant radiotherapy use, ~10% loss to follow-up without sensitivity analysis, and early stopping for benefit after an unplanned interim analysis with reporting of only the first 500 of 596 randomized patients.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a prospective randomized trial with stratification by T stage and random allocation to resection alone versus resection plus elective supraomohyoid neck dissection: "All 67 patients were stratified by stage, T1, N0; and T2, N0; and those in each stage were randomized to receive 1 of 2 types of treatment."

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization with stratification by T stage is asserted, but no method of sequence generation or allocation concealment is described, and no baseline table by treatment arm is presented (distributions of stage, site, and tumor thickness within RA vs RSOND are not reported), so comparability cannot be verified.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All 67 patients were stratified by stage, T1, N0; and T2, N0; and those in each stage were randomized to receive 1 of 2 types of treatment: resection alone (RA) or resection plus elective supraomohyoid neck dissection (RSOND)."

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding is impossible in a surgical trial and co-interventions (post-operative versus palliative radiotherapy) differed between arms; no statement of intention-to-treat analysis, crossovers, or protocol deviations (e.g., patients in the RA arm who refused or received delayed dissection) is provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "In our study, a low number of patients received radiotherapy: 7 patients (21%) of the RSOND group and 10 (30%) in the RA group. In the latter group, palliative radiotherapy was delivered to 8 of the 10 patients."

domain_judgments.rationale: All 67 randomized patients appear accounted for in the recurrence and survival analyses, but no information is given on losses to follow-up, censoring, or completeness of follow-up duration, and the description of patients returning late with advanced disease suggests irregular follow-up that could differ between arms (particularly in the "wait and see" RA arm).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This may be explained because this prospective study included a large number of low socioeconomic level patients who had returned to follow-up with advanced neck recurrence."

domain_judgments.rationale: Recurrence and survival are fairly objective outcomes assessed histologically, but outcome assessors were necessarily unblinded, and detection of neck disease is inherently asymmetric between arms (RSOND patients had pathological nodal staging and adjuvant radiotherapy while RA patients were detected clinically on follow-up), which can bias the comparison of neck recurrence and disease-free survival.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All patients had the primary lesion and cervical lymph nodes examined by microscopic analysis of frozen sections."

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or pre-specified primary outcome is reported; multiple outcomes (locoregional failure, neck recurrence, occult metastasis, disease-free and overall survival) and multiple subgroup analyses (sex, age, site, stage, thickness dichotomized at the data-derived mean of 4 mm) were tested with borderline P values (P = 0.05), and the headline conclusion rests on a post hoc subgroup, indicating selective reporting of favourable analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Patients with tumor thickness >4 mm treated by RSOND had significant benefit on disease-free survival (P = 0.05)."

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by Domain 5: there is no pre-specified protocol or primary outcome, the key conclusion rests on a post hoc subgroup defined by a data-derived 4 mm thickness cut-off, and multiple borderline (P = 0.05) analyses are reported. This is compounded by some concerns in all other domains — unspecified sequence generation/allocation concealment with no baseline comparison by arm, unblinded surgical interventions with differential radiotherapy co-interventions, unreported follow-up completeness, and asymmetric outcome ascertainment favouring the dissection arm.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly states that eligible T1-2 N0M0 patients were "randomized from previously generated random numbers" to hemiglossectomy alone versus hemiglossectomy plus ipsilateral radical neck dissection, i.e., an explicit random allocation sequence.

domain_judgments.rationale: A random sequence was generated, but there is no description of allocation concealment, and the analysed groups are markedly unequal in size (21 vs 14, with 15 vs 8 T2 tumours), raising doubt about concealment/baseline balance.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "randomized from previously generated random numbers to either hemiglossectomy alone (group A) or hemiglossectomy and ipsilateral radical neck dissection (group B)"

domain_judgments.rationale: Surgical interventions were necessarily unblinded, 14 randomized patients never received the allocated treatment and were excluded, and the analysis was per-protocol (only treated patients) rather than intention-to-treat; co-interventions (postoperative radiotherapy) were applied based on pathology rather than protocolised equally.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Twelve patients did not take treatment after entry and two patients were declared unfit for surgery."

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 35 of 73 randomized patients (48%) contributed outcome data in this interim report, with 14 untreated/unfit excluded and 24 further excluded for insufficient follow-up, and no analysis or sensitivity assessment of the impact of these large exclusions by arm is provided.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of 73 patients have been entered into the protocol to date... Thirty-five of these patients who have completed a minimum of 1 year of follow-up after completion of treatment have been analysed."

domain_judgments.rationale: Disease-free survival/recurrence is a fairly objective outcome, but detection of nodal recurrence was by unblinded clinical follow-up performed by one of the trial authors who knew the assigned surgery, and detection effort could differ between arms (operated vs observed necks).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "All patients were personally followed by one of the authors (A.R.F.)."

domain_judgments.rationale: This is an unplanned/unspecified interim analysis of an ongoing trial with no available protocol or pre-specified analysis plan, no stated primary outcome or statistical methods, and multiple subgroup results (e.g., pathologically node-positive subgroup, contralateral nodal failure) reported selectively.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "This paper presents the first report of an ongoing prospective randomised clinical trial... The study commenced in July 1985 and will continue until 100 patients have been accessioned."

overall_summary: Although allocation used previously generated random numbers, this is an unplanned interim report in which only 35 of 73 randomized patients (48%) were analysed, with per-protocol exclusion of untreated patients and no handling of missing data, plus no pre-specified protocol, primary outcome, or statistical methods. The high risk in missing outcome data (D3) and selective reporting (D5), compounded by unblinded outcome assessment by a trial author, drives an overall high risk of bias.
